commitResults.messageBody:
Duke.java: Rename the Java file and add a few new features

Duke.java is the default file provided in the project template and needs to be modified to make it more unique and boast more features.

Renaming the file to Sallybot.java, as well as modifying the greeting message and the ASCII text that is displayed along with it and adding an exit message.

The Duke Chatbot name is only a placeholder, and the project has since been renamed Sallybot, named after the Japanese-American voice actress Sally Amaki. Consequently, the greeting message has to be modified to reflect the change. A goodbye message is added to add more depth and friendliness.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level 1: Add Echo and command messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Sallybot.java: Repeat a string message that a user types in the CLI, sends the goodbye message when the command "bye" is entered.

The previous iteration of Sallybot only had hello and bye messages and lacked interaction with the user via user input.

Here, we add a Scanner input that takes a string entered by the user, and prints that exact same string on the CLI. We add a while loop to constantly prompt the user to enter a message until the command "bye" is sent. We use a case statement to handle the commands entered by the user, and the case block handles the break from the while loop when "bye" is entered such that the program quits.

To provide users with the choice of constantly entering messages without needing to restart the application each time a message is entered, a while loop is used. We expect more commands to be introduced, so a case statement is utilised.

In addition, the content of the greeting and bye messages have been modified to better reflect the intended character of Sallybot, which follows the personality of its namesake.

So far, Sallybot has only a few main features, greet the user, take in user input and exit when the command "bye" is entered.

Sallybot needs more features to be more useful and appealing to users. New features need to be introduced to achieve this.

We add the functionality to store text into a dynamic array that stores tasks instead of merely echoing them, so users can use Sallybot to store their lists of to-dos. We introduce the command "list" to list out all tasks stored in the array so far.

Doing so adds the purpose of taking down tasks and to-dos to Sallybot, contributing to its utility.

Add the ability to mark tasks as done and change the status back to not done.

Previously, the task list had no capability of marking and displaying a task as completed or not.

We add new class Task to create task objects that come with a description and a status that indicates the completion status of a task, as well as new commands "mark [index of task]" and "unmark [index of task]" to mark a task at a certain index as done or not done respectively.

This adds more customizability and immersion to the Tasks feature of Sallybot.

Minor additions such as Javadoc comments have been added.

Verify all the code in the files comply with the CS2113 coding standards.

A few parts of the code were not compliant with the CS2113 coding standards.

We rectify the try-catch statement and rename a Boolean variable.

Now, the code follows the coding standards.

Add functionality for different types of tasks to Sallybot.

At this juncture, Sallybot is able to keep track of tasks, but not specialised ones such as deadlines which have a date/time specified. Sallybot does not also state the number of tasks remaining.

Here, we create new ToDo, Deadline and Event subclasses that inherit from the Task class, each inheriting features from the parent class as well as having their own features such as Event having from and to String variables to take note of the starting and ending dates.

Doing so adds better organisation of tasks and adds more functionality to the task tracking feature of Sallybot and thus adding more dynamism to Sallybot.

In addition, some UI improvements have been implemented.

Tested Sallybot using the I/O redirection technique.

Previously, there was no automated or semi-automated testing done on Sallybot, only manual testing.

We make slight modifications to the runtest.bat and runtest.sh files, put in some commands for testing in input.txt, and modify the file EXPECTED.TXT to include the expected output. After which, we run either 1 of the runtest files to obtain ACTUAL.TXT, which is then compared to EXPECTED.TXT using the automatic batch file.

This allows us to find any inconsistencies in the output that Sallybot gives as opposed to the ideal output with ease, and make the necessary rectifications.

From the tests, it was determined that putting the Scanner definition in the while loop in Sallybot.java was unideal as it caused errors during the automated testing, so it was moved out of the loop.

Improve the code quality according to the recommendations given by CS2113 to Sallybot.

Previously, some of the code in Sallybot had poor readability, block organisation and needed refactoring.

We extract a few methods from the case statement in Sallybot.java, as well as tweak and add Javadoc comments and regular comments that were clear and met the standards. We also consolidate duplicate fragments in conditional statements

These improve the overall readability, organisation and flow of Java class files in Sallybot, enabling other users to see the contents with ease.

Update the contents in README.md to better describe Sallybot.

Previously, the README.md contained info about the Duke chatbot that came with the project template. That is no longer accurate as the template Sallybot is based on has been heavily modified to become Sallybot.

We change the description of Sallybot and change the output it will give in the README.md file to better reflect its nature.

Users will now be able to understand Sallybot better, its origins and how to use it.

Program Sallybot to handle incorrect commands and inputs entered by the user.

Previously, Sallybot could not deal with most erroneous input and would still take in commands with the incorrect format. For instance, entering deadline without a task title and by date would still be accepted and displayed in the list of items with empty content. There were only a few blocks of code that handled NumberFormatException errors for marking and unmarking items.

We add a new exception class, SallyException, to handle and reject commands that are entered with incorrect formatting or empty parameters, and when invalid commands are entered.

This way, all input will be handled properly such that Sallybot can continue to run and prompt users without any errors stopping the program when running, or experience any anomalous input processed.

Additionally, new helper functions have been created, such as processEvent, to streamline and neaten the code.

Organise the classes into suitable Java packages.

Initially all files were in a single java folder and were not in separate packages.

Move core classes into package structure: SallyException -> sallybot.exception, Task/ToDo/Deadline/Event -> sallybot.task, and Sallybot -> sallybot.ui. Added corresponding package declarations and updated imports in Sallybot.java.

No functional changes—just filesystem/package refactor to match Java packaging conventions.

Remove redundant 'return' statements in Sallybot.java

Some return statements were either unreachable after a thrown SallyException or redundant at the end of catch blocks.

Remove unnecessary `return;` statements in src/main/java/sallybot/ui/Sallybot.java. The removed returns were either unreachable after a thrown SallyException or redundant at the end of catch blocks.

This cleans up the code by eliminating dead statements and improving readability.

Level 6: Add support for deletion of tasks.

Originally, there was no way tasks could be removed from the list.

Implement a 'delete' command with a new processDelete method that uses functions that come with ArrayList to remove items by index from the list.

Now tasks can be removed easily using the index indicated in the list of tasks.

Additionally, a help command is implemented to list the available commands.

Level 7: Add storage and load/save functions

Previously, there was no way of storing task data locally. Any data logged during the execution of Sallybot would be discarded once Sallybot terminates.

Introduce Storage class to persist tasks to data/sallybot.txt (create dirs, read/write UTF-8, parse/encode T/D/E lines and skip corrupted lines). Add sample data/sallybot.txt. Add getters on Task/Deadline/Event (getIsDone, getBy, getFrom, getTo) to support encoding. Integrate Storage into Sallybot: load tasks at startup and save after task modifications; minor exception message formatting tweak.

Users can hence create a text file, sallybot.txt, to write down their list of tasks to feed into Sallybot and use the file to store data. A text file will be created if no file exists.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add local storage of tasks for delete command
commitResults.messageBody:
Added support for deletion of tasks to be reflected in file storage.

Previously when the branches Level-6 and Level-7 were merged, there was no saving for the delete function.

the processDelete method in Sallybot.java is now capable of saving the array of tasks into a TXT file with the help of STORAGE.save.

Users can now see their tasks being successfully deleted and reflected in their TXT file of tasks.

Additional changes include introduce TaskInterface and have Task implement it (with @Override annotations) to formalise the Task API. Move Sallybot class package from sallybot.ui to sallybot.

Added Javadoc comments to most classes and functions.

Even though some classes and methods already had Javadoc comments before, new methods and classes have popped up since, leading to a majority of them not having Javadoc comments.

Introduce Javadoc comments across core classes (Sallybot, Storage, Task, TaskInterface, ToDo, Deadline, Event), providing descriptions of each class and method and how that work.

Users have a clearer idea of how the methods and classes are used, what parameters are thrown into and how to properly call them.

Additionally, minor changes have been made to ensure compliance with CS2113 coding standards, such as fixing the indentation of the switch statement in Storage.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Parser, TaskList, and Ui classes
commitResults.messageBody:
A-MoreOOP: Use More OOP to make the code more OOP.

While parts of the code like tasks were already OOP, there was still room for improvement with regards to OOP.

Introduce Parser, TaskList and Ui classes and refactor Sallybot to use them. Sallybot is converted to an instance-based entrypoint (Sallybot(String)) that delegates input/output to Ui, parsing to Parser, and task management to TaskList. Rewrite command handlers to use the new APIs and storage.save now accepts an unmodifiable list. Add Parser utilities for splitting todo/deadline/event input and a robust ParsedCommand record. Ui centralises all console output and input handling (including welcome/help/bye/error/list formatting).

Overall, making Sallybot more object-oriented improves separation of concerns, readability and testability.

README was updated to reflect changes made to Sallybot.

A-MoreOOP: Added new command package with separate command classes for each available command of Sallybot.

While more OOP was already achieved in the last commit, the commands of Sallybot were not made object-oriented. There hence existed an area for improvement in making the code more object-oriented.

Extract command handling into sallybot.commands (Command, CommandResult and concrete commands such as AddTodoCommand, AddDeadlineCommand, AddEventCommand, ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, HelpCommand, ByeCommand, UnknownCommand). Make Parser.parse return a Command object instead of a ParsedCommand, and simplify Sallybot to execute commands and react to CommandResult (save/exit).

This achieves a clearer object-oriented format that paves a way for addition of new commands that follow the Command class format, while preserving the logic of Sallybot and its validation and save behaviour.

Also updated test harness by improving runtest.bat to generate a sources list and invoke javac/java with the correct package/classpath.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Level 8: Add the ability of parsing dates and times stored in storage text file and display them in the CLI and handle dates and times inserted using Deadline and Event commands to store them in a standardised format.

Previously, deadline and event commands could take any arguments for their /from, /to and /by subcommands, which are supposed to be storing dates and/or times.

Introduce DateTimeUtil for parsing/formatting user and storage datetimes and switch Deadline/Event to use LocalDateTime. Update Storage to read/write ISO-8601 datetimes and skip corrupted lines, adjust Parser to split on literal subcommands without breaking dates, and update AddDeadlineCommand/AddEventCommand files to validate and parse dates via DateTimeUtil.

Now, users must input dates and/or times for deadline and event commands, preferably in the recommended date format of d/m/yyyy or yyyy-mm-dd and 24hr time format, even though datetimes such as "Monday 4pm" will still be accepted.

Also add backward-compatible constructors for loading, polish Ui/Sallybot Javadoc, and update test/data fixtures to use the new datetime formats.
Add support for dates and times

Level 9. Find: Give users a way to find a task by searching for a keyword in the task description.

Prior to this commit, there was no way for users to search for their tasks using keywords.

Add FindCommand to locate tasks by keyword, produce UI output, and return a non-action result. Update Parser to recognize the "find" command and add parseKeyword helper to extract the search term. Add TaskList.find(...) to search stored tasks and throw a SallyException when no matches are found. These changes wire up keyword search end-to-end and standardise command behavior.

Now, users can search for their tasks using a keyword or a sentence with the find command.

Additionally, introduce CommandInterface (execute/isExit) and make abstract Command implement it with a default isExit() implementation.
Add find command
